disable_high_voltage.answer: Disabling direct HV hazards: Open the hood and locate the First Responder Loop. Double cut the First Responder Loop to interrupt HV power. Then disconnect the 48V battery. Do not cut or open the high voltage cables themselves. After disabling, ensure all power sources are isolated and proceed with safe extrication using PPE. If vehicle is submerged or damaged, monitor HV battery temperature and maintain no direct contact with orange-insulated cables. Do not push on HV battery. Keep a clear, safe perimeter and avoid energizing components during stabilization.

images.desc: Disabling HV hazards: First Responder Loop and 48V battery disconnect

avoid_hv_cable_cutting.answer: Never cut or open high voltage components or cables. All high voltage cables have orange insulation and cutting these can cause severe injury or fire. Follow the disconnection steps for HV power and maintain PPE. If a collision has compromised energy systems, rely on the First Responder Loop and HV isolation steps instead of cutting cables.
